Under these rules, banks operating in the country are now required to conduct independent reviews of any upcoming AI projects prior to their official implementation. This measure aims to ensure robust risk management and governance as the financial sector increasingly adopts advanced technologies.
content_ta: சிங்கப்பூர் central bank, நிதி நிறுவனங்களின் artificial intelligence பயன்பாடு குறித்த புதிய விதிமுறைகளை வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய விதிகளின்படி, நாட்டில் செயல்படும் banks, தங்களின் வரவிருக்கும் எந்தவொரு AI திட்டங்களையும் நடைமுறைப்படுத்துவதற்கு முன்பு ஒரு independent review பெற வேண்டும் என்று கட்டாயமாக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. நிதித் துறையில் மேம்பட்ட தொழில்நுட்பங்கள் அதிகளவில் ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளப்பட்டு வருவதால், வலுவான risk management மற்றும் governance-ஐ உறுதி செய்வதை இந்த நடவடிக்கை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Facephi strengthens global presence through partnership with credit bureau Crif
summary: Facephi (BME Growth: FACE; Euronext Growth Paris: ALPHI), a global leader in digital identity verification and fraud prevention, today announced that it has entered into a strategic partnership with CRIF, a global company specialising in credit information, risk management and digital solutions, with operations in 37 countries.
content: Digital identity verification and fraud prevention leader Facephi has announced a strategic partnership with global credit information and risk management company CRIF. This collaboration aims to strengthen Facephi's global market presence by combining its verification expertise with CRIF's extensive international operations spanning 37 countries.
content_ta: டிஜிட்டல் அடையாள சரிபார்ப்பு மற்றும் மோசடி தடுப்பு நிறுவனமான Facephi, கடன் தகவல் மற்றும் மேலாண்மை நிறுவனமான CRIF உடன் ஒரு முக்கிய கூட்டாண்மையை அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த ஒத்துழைப்பு 37 நாடுகளில் இயங்கும் CRIF இன் சர்வதேச வலையமைப்பின் மூலம் Facephi இன் உலகளாவிய இருப்பை பலப்படுத்தும்.

title: Murex platform connects to ICE market data feed
summary: Murex, the global leader in trading, risk management and post trade solutions for capital markets, is pleased to announce that its MX.3 platform can now be natively connected to Intercontinental Exchange’s (ICE) real time market data feed, the ICE Consolidated Feed.
content: Murex, a global leader in trading, risk management, and post-trade solutions, has announced that its MX.3 platform now connects natively to the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) real-time market data feed. This integration allows users of the ICE Consolidated Feed to access comprehensive data directly through the Murex platform, enhancing trading and risk management capabilities for capital markets participants.
content_ta: Trading, risk management மற்றும் post-trade solutions துறையில் முன்னணி நிறுவனமான Murex, தனது MX.3 platform-ஐ Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)-ன் real-time market data feed-டன் natively இணைக்க முடிவதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த integration மூலமாக, ICE Consolidated Feed பயனர்கள் Murex platform வழியாக நேரடியாக தரவுகளைப் பெற்று, capital markets-க்கான வர்த்தக மற்றும் risk management திறன்களை மேம்படுத்த முடியும்.

title: PawaPay secures Mozambique payment licence
summary: PawaPay, a leading pan-African payments aggregator, has been granted a Payment Service Provider (PSP) licence by the Bank of Mozambique through its local subsidiary, Quidexplus Mozambique.
content: PawaPay, a leading pan-African payments aggregator, has officially secured a Payment Service Provider licence from the Bank of Mozambique. The approval was granted through its local subsidiary, Quidexplus Mozambique. This regulatory milestone allows the company to expand its payment services and strengthen its operations within the Mozambican market, supporting the growth of digital transactions across the region.
content_ta: முன்னணி பான்-ஆப்பிரிக்கா கட்டண aggregato-ரான PawaPay, மொசாம்பிக் வங்கியிடமிருந்து Payment Service Provider (PSP) உரிமத்தை அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாகப் பெற்றுள்ளது. இதன் உள்ளூர் துணை நிறுவனமான Quidexplus Mozambique மூலம் இந்த அனுமதி வழங்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த ஒழுங்குமுறை மைல்கல் அந்நிறுவனம் தனது கட்டண சேவைகளை விரிவுபடுத்தவும், அப்பகுதியில் டிஜிட்டல் பரிவர்த்தனைகளின் வளர்ச்சியை ஆதரிக்கவும் உதவுகிறது.

title: Combatting the Rise of AI-Driven Financial Crime in Banking
summary: At Sibos 2026, FICO’s Julie Conroy reveals how banks can use agentic AI and cloud tech to combat deepfakes and rising financial crime that targets wealth management and corporate clients.
content: At Sibos 2026, FICO expert Julie Conroy discussed strategies for banks to combat the rising threat of AI-driven financial crime. As fraudsters increasingly target wealth management and corporate clients with advanced techniques like deepfakes, financial institutions are being urged to adopt agentic AI and cloud technologies to protect their systems and secure customer assets.
content_ta: Sibos 2026 மாநாட்டில், FICO நிறுவனத்தைச் சேர்ந்த Julie Conroy, AI தொழில்நுட்பம் மூலம் அதிகரிக்கும் நிதி மோசடிகளை வங்கிகள் எவ்வாறு எதிர்கொள்வது என்பது குறித்து விவரித்தார். டீப்கேக் (deepfakes) போன்ற அதிநவீன முறைகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி செல்வம் மேலாண்மை மற்றும் கார்ப்பரேட் வாடிக்கையாளர்களை மோசடி செய்பவர்கள் குறிவைப்பதால், வங்கிகள் ஏஜென்டிக் AI மற்றும் கிளவுட் தொழில்நுட்பங்களைப் பயன்படுத்தி தங்கள் பாதுகாப்பை பலப்படுத்த வேண்டும் என்று அறிவுறுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Deposits and stablecoins: The complete digital money proposition for banks
summary: What does programmable money solve for clients, and what remains a matter of regulation and capital controls?
content: Digital money propositions for banks now encompass both traditional deposits and stablecoins. This combination offers clients programmable money solutions that streamline transactions and automate complex financial workflows. However, widespread adoption and full implementation continue to depend heavily on evolving regulatory frameworks and cross-border capital controls.
content_ta: வங்கிகளுக்கான டிஜிட்டல் பண சேவைகளில் இப்போது பாரம்பரிய டெபாசிட்டுகள் மற்றும் stablecoins இரண்டும் அடங்கும். இந்த kombinasyon வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு புரோகிராம் செய்யக்கூடிய பண தீர்வுகளை வழங்குகிறது, இது பரிவர்த்தனைகளை எளிதாக்குகிறது. இருப்பினும், இதன் பரவலான பயன்பாடு மற்றும் முழுமையான அமலாக்கம் ஆகியவை ஒழுங்குமுறைச் சட்டங்கள் மற்றும் மூலதனக் கட்டுப்பாடுகளைப் பொறுத்தே அமைகின்றன.

title: The Future of RWA Payment Rails: Tokenization, Stablecoins and Programmable Finance
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: The intersection of tokenization, stablecoins, and programmable finance is shaping the future of RWA payment rails. According to community insights on Finextra, these technological advancements are transforming traditional transaction systems. By leveraging blockchain infrastructure, financial institutions and networks are exploring more efficient, transparent, and automated settlement processes for real-world assets in the evolving digital economy.
content_ta: டோக்கனைசேஷன், stablecoins மற்றும் புரோகிராமபில் ஃபைனான்ஸ் ஆகியவற்றின் ஒருங்கிணைப்பு RWA பேமெண்ட் ரெயில்களின் எதிர்காலத்தை வடிவமைக்கிறது. Finextra சமூகக் கருத்துகளின்படி, இந்த தொழில்நுட்ப வளர்ச்சிகள் பாரம்பரிய பரிவர்த்தனை முறைகளை மாற்றி அமைக்கின்றன. பிளாக்செயின் கட்டமைப்பைப் பயன்படுத்துவதன் மூலம், நிதிய நிறுவனங்கள் மற்றும் நெட்வொர்க்குகள் மிகவும் திறமையான, வெளிப்படையான மற்றும் தானியங்கு தீர்வு செயல்முறைகளை ஆராய்ந்து வருகின்றன.

title: Temenos At Sibos 2026: The Switchable Middle, The Four Musketeers And What Banks Must Fix Next
summary:
Temenos executives Will Moroney and Mick Fennell talk to The Fintech Times at Sibos 2026 about the switchable middle, AI and core modernisation, agentic payments and tokenised money.

title: Vaults: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
summary: Everyone keeps asking the SEC what a vault is. More useful question: what should a vault be, now that the constraints that produced the shared-vault container no longer exist? Billions sit in these things. Banks and fintechs are shopping. Regulators are circling. The industry is... Read More
content: Regulators and financial institutions are increasingly focusing on the definition and function of vaults in the digital asset space. Billions of dollars currently sit in these containers as banks and fintech firms evaluate their options. Experts note that the constraints which originally shaped shared-vault designs no longer apply, raising questions about what these structures should become as regulatory scrutiny grows.
content_ta: டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சந்தையில் Vaults-களின் வரையறை மற்றும் செயல்பாடு குறித்து ரெகுலேட்டர்கள் மற்றும் நிதி நிறுவனங்களின் கவனம் அதிகரித்து வருகிறது. வங்கிகளும் fintech நிறுவனங்களும் தங்கள் விருப்பங்களை ஆராய்ந்து வருவதால், இந்த அமைப்புகளில் தற்போது பல பில்லியன் டляர்கள் உள்ளன. ஷேர்டு-வால்ட் வடிவமைப்புகளை உருவாக்கிய கட்டுப்பாடுகள் இனி பொருந்தாது என்பதால், ரெகுலேட்டர்களின் கண்காணிப்பு அதிகரிக்கும் போது இந்த கட்டமைப்புகள் எவ்வாறு மாற வேண்டும் என்ற கேள்விகள் எழுந்துள்ளன.

title: Finance leaders fight deepfakes

According to a new survey conducted by Early Warning Services’ Certos, finance leaders are actively working to combat these advanced digital deception techniques. As artificial intelligence technology evolves, organizations must adapt their security measures to protect corporate assets and prevent sophisticated financial scams targeting their systems.
content_ta: கார்ப்பரேட் நிதித்துறைகள் AI-அம்சங்களுடன் கூடிய மோசடிகள் மற்றும் டீப்ஃபேக்குகளின் அச்சுறுத்தல்களைத் தொடர்ந்து எதிர்கொண்டு வருகின்றன. Early Warning Services இன் Certos நடத்திய புதிய ஆய்வின்படி, இந்த மேம்பட்ட டிஜிட்டல் ஏமாற்று முறைகளை எதிர்த்துப் போராட நிதித்துறை தலைவர்கள் தீவிரமாகச் செயல்பட்டு வருகின்றனர். செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு தொழில்நுட்பம் வளர்ந்து வருவதால், நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் சொத்துக்களைப் பாதுகாக்கப் பாதுகாப்பு நடவடிக்கைகளை மேம்படுத்த வேண்டும்.

title: BBVA Embarks on a New Growth Phase in Spain, with Customers at Its Heart and AI at the Forefront
summary:
BBVA is entering a new phase from a position of leadership and credibility, following years of transforming its business model and building relationships with its customers. In the current environment, the bank aims to accelerate its growth in Spain by focusing on three levers: expanding its customer base, deepening customer relationships and increasing its presence in higher-value businesses such as the enterprise segments, insurance and Global Wealth. Artificial Intelligence (AI) will be the key accelerator in this new phase, with customers at the heart of the transformation and an increasingly simple, hyper-personalized and specialized experience. This was highlighted by BBVA’s country manager in Spain, Peio Belausteguigoitia, during a meeting with analysts and investors.
 








In terms of customer growth, in 2025, BBVA added 962,000 retail customers in Spain and a further 68,000 business customers, representing 2 times and 1.3 times, respectively, the acquisition rates recorded in 2019. Of these new customers, 70% make BBVA their main bank within the first six months.
The bank has set itself the goal of further improving customer experience and ensuring that these relationships generate greater value from the outset. Indeed, the revenue generated by a primary customer increases 3.7-fold on average over five years. In the case of enterprise clients, customers that maintain a primary banking relationship with BBVA generate twice as much revenue as those with a less engaged relationship.
In enterprise segments, BBVA aims to become its customers’ strategic partner and play a more relevant role in their day-to-day operations. To achieve this goal, the bank is working on developing transactional solutions —such as payroll and tax payments and foreign trade-related solutions— and increasingly secure digital services to provide a better customer experience. At the same time, it is harnessing the potential of AI to simplify and accelerate processes and provide increasingly specialized advice, BBVA’s country manager explained.
Peio Belausteguigoitia said that the strategy will be tailored to the specific needs of each segment and each company. In the SME segment, where BBVA led customer acquisition in 2025 — one in four new SMEs that opened an account in Spain did so with the bank — BBVA will continue to strengthen digital and remote engagement, which is particularly valued by these customers, while developing sector-specific propositions.
For larger companies, it will strengthen specialized advisory services and use AI-based tools to expand relationship managers’ capabilities and simplify processes. For large corporations, the focus will be on deepening relationships, with cross-border business and sustainability as the main growth levers, while continuing to develop sector-specific advisory capabilities.
Another business where BBVA’s head of Spain sees growth potential is insurance: only 21% of customers have an insurance policy with the bank, a figure BBVA aims to increase through its strategic partnerships in the non-life segments, where BBVA is already growing faster than the market. Premiums in these segments grew by 18% between 2021 and 2025, compared with 7% for the market. BBVA now aims to move forward with a more personalized offering, anticipating its customers’ protection needs, with simpler and more agile processes and new products in areas such as health, home, cyber risk and enterprises.
 
‘Global Wealth’ will be another priority growth area in this strategic cycle, he highlighted. In Spain, BBVA has 201,000 private banking and wealth management clients, an 84% satisfaction rate in this segment and 46% more bankers than in December 2020. Looking ahead, the bank will continue to expand its value proposition thanks to AI. AI will also make it possible to extend advisory capabilities and simplify servicing and administrative tasks.
AI, the key accelerator of the new phase
BBVA’s country manager placed particular emphasis on the fact that AI will cut across this strategy. Across the bank as a whole, this technology will help simplify and automate processes and develop a more robust, efficient and scalable model, he said.
Customers will remain at the heart of this transformation, with their experience central to every decision, Peio Belausteguigoitia stressed. He noted that AI expands and enhances what the bank can do for its customers, enabling increasingly personalized service for each individual and company and helping deliver a unique experience.
This means evolving from propositions designed for groups of customers towards an increasingly individualized relationship, capable of using each person’s interactions and needs to provide responses that are more relevant to their specific circumstances. The goal is for technology to make customers’ day-to-day relationship with the bank easier without losing the specialization and more technical advice they need when required, he added.
“We believe we are on the right path to continue building a new bank. This transformation will have a significant impact on both the way we work and the way we engage with our customers, resulting in a significant improvement in their experience,” BBVA’s country manager in Spain said.
 
NoYesBanking08 Oct, 2026

title: New Rules to Make Long-Term Investment Funds Clearer
summary:
This will help give the market more confidence to invest in funds that support private markets.
The new rules mean that investors will have to give 90 days' notice to access their funds but will be more certain that they will receive their money.
For investors, this means the fund should be clearer from the start about how quickly they can get their money back and whether the fund is right for their needs.
Currently some of these funds allow people to take money out daily with no notice period. During periods of stress or volatility there is a risk that some funds may suspend all payments due to lack of available cash. Some are also holding extra cash, leaving less invested in their intended assets.
Rushed sales can lower prices, harm investors who stay invested and put pressure on markets.
The new notice period would give managers time to sell assets in an orderly way and make liquidity-driven suspensions less likely.
Existing funds would have 2 years to comply and give investors at least 1 year’s notice.
The proposals bring the UK into line with new international liquidity standards for open ended funds.
Michelle Beck, director, markets, at the FCA, said: 'Funds should be clear about whether they offer quick access or are built for longer-term investments like property. Our rules will help firms make that clearer and give the market more confidence to invest.'

title: Samsung Wallet to Bring Stablecoin Access to Eligible Galaxy Users in the US
summary:
Samsung Electronics America today announced that stablecoin wallet functionality will launch in Samsung Wallet starting in the last week of October for eligible Galaxy users in the United States, bringing eligible cross-border stablecoin transfers into the app they already use regularly.
The feature will initially support USDC, a U.S. dollar-denominated stablecoin.
“Sending money abroad should feel as convenient as using the wallet already on your phone,” said Woncheol Chai, EVP and Head of the Digital Wallet Team at the Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics. “We’re bringing USDC transfers into Samsung Wallet so eligible Galaxy users can get started without installing another app or managing private keys themselves.”
 




Integrating Stablecoin Access into Samsung Wallet
By integrating stablecoin functionality natively into Galaxy devices via Samsung Wallet, Samsung is removing some of the hassle typically associated with stablecoin use, such as installing separate crypto apps, creating wallets, and managing private keys. At launch, the feature will be available across 82 million U.S. Galaxy devices.
The launch marks the next chapter of Samsung and Coinbase’s collaboration, following the addition of Samsung Pay as a payment option in the Coinbase app and access to Coinbase One benefits for eligible users through Samsung Wallet.
Convenient Money Transfers Across Global Borders     
Eligible Galaxy users will be able to send USDC directly from Samsung Wallet to compatible crypto wallets internationally in seconds and with no transfer fees. Whether splitting travel expenses or sending money to friends, eligible users can transfer USDC conveniently from their Galaxy devices.
Samsung Wallet will also enable eligible users to send money to qualifying bank accounts in more than 60 countries, with funds delivered in the recipient’s local currency. This offers a convenient way to send money from Samsung Wallet, with eligible recipients receiving funds directly in their bank accounts without needing a crypto wallet. By making international transfers more convenient, Samsung is helping move stablecoins like USDC from a specialized crypto tool toward a more practical way for eligible Galaxy users to send money.
Built-In Security and Compliance Powered by Bastion and Coinbase Prime
Samsung is launching the feature following the establishment of a regulatory framework for stablecoins. Bastion, a licensed stablecoin custodian and infrastructure provider overseen by U.S. financial regulators, will power the cross-border payment framework for Samsung Wallet’s new stablecoin capabilities. To secure these assets, Bastion has partnered with Coinbase as its official sub-custodian, safeguarding all USDC in Samsung Wallet via Coinbase Prime Vault. Samsung Galaxy devices compatible with the stablecoin functionality act as the secure gateway, requiring biometric authentication on registered devices to initiate transfers.
USDC will be the first supported stablecoin by Samsung Wallet, with USDC functionality operated together with Bastion and Coinbase. When users select “Buy Stablecoin,” USDC will appear as the default dollar stablecoin. Additional aspects of the service—including infrastructure and blockchain network support—will be provided by separate partners with the required technical capabilities, including Solana and Sui.
Future capabilities may include the ability for eligible users to pay with stablecoins online or by tapping an eligible Galaxy device in store, followed by potential expansion into additional markets in line with regulatory developments in each country.

title: Mastercard to Keep Payments Moving During Power and Network Outages Across Europe
summary:
From early 2027, Mastercard’s new offline payment requirements will help people across Europe continue to pay when power or network connections fail.
When a power blackout hit Spain and Portugal in April 2025, an estimated 55 million people were suddenly unable to make digital payments. Today, Mastercard announced new offline payment requirements across its European network, designed to keep money moving and payments working when power or network connections fail.
From February 2027, all newly issued Mastercard cards across Europe will be enabled to make offline payments. By May 2027, all new and replacement payment terminals will also be required to support them.
Once the requirements are implemented across Europe, people will be able to use chip and PIN during an outage to pay for essentials at supermarkets, grocery stores, service stations and pharmacies, as well as at travel and ticket machines.
Offline payments work by securely storing spending limits on a card’s chip. If a terminal loses its connection, the transaction can be approved locally, up to a limit of €200 per transaction set in advance by the cardholder’s bank. It is then submitted for clearing when the connection is restored.
Mastercard has already successfully implemented offline payments in Denmark, Sweden, Estonia and Latvia. During a recent storm in Latvia, card payments continued in shops powered by local generators. In Denmark this spring, when a technical outage isolated terminals from the wider payment system, Mastercard’s crisis procedures enabled many transactions to continue at critical merchants.
Following coordination with partners, national governments, regulators and central banks, Mastercard is now expanding the capability more widely across Europe.
The rollout builds on steps Mastercard has taken over the past 12 months including investment in local infrastructure and cybersecurity—to strengthen the resilience of Europe’s payment networks.
“When the power or network goes down, people still need to buy food, fuel and medicine,” said Brice van de Walle, Executive Vice President, Core Payments at Mastercard. “We’ve seen that offline payments can make a real difference. By expanding this technology across Europe, we can help people keep paying for the things they need, even when the unexpected happens.”

title: BNY Expands Digital Asset Custody Platform in Europe
summary:
BNY, a global financial services company, today announced the expansion of its Digital Asset Custody platform for select institutions in the European Union under the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework, making BNY one of the first global systemically important banks to offer regulated digital asset custody in the region.
The expansion follows the addition of The Bank of New York Mellon SA/NV, BNY's European banking entity, to the European Securities and Markets Authority MiCA register in July 2026 — enabling BNY to provide custody, administration, and transfer services for crypto-assets on behalf of clients in one of the world's largest regulated markets for digital assets.
“Digital asset adoption is accelerating across Europe — from banks and broker-dealers expanding crypto-asset and stablecoin offerings to asset managers and corporate treasurers exploring digital payments and tokenized securities to enhance liquidity, settlement and collateral mobility,” said Jennifer Barker, Head of Europe at BNY. “To support increasingly digital strategies, institutions need solutions with the same resilience, oversight and safeguards they rely on across traditional operations. By expanding our platform in Europe, we are providing clients with institutional-grade infrastructure to navigate this transition with confidence.”
Secure and regulated digital asset custody
Launched in 2022, BNY’s Digital Asset Custody platform offers secure safekeeping and servicing of digital assets through infrastructure designed with risk management and security controls, including multiparty computation technology, segregated client wallets and storage of private keys.
Through a well-developed custody model, BNY can provide market participants with regulated access to assets including BTC, ETH, SOL and USDC with ambitions to support broader crypto-assets and stablecoins.
“Our platform isn’t a standalone solution — we built it drawing from the deep expertise, rigorous controls and unwavering commitment to client trust that underpins our existing asset servicing franchise,” said Emily Portney, Global Head of Asset Servicing at BNY. “As we expand this capability, we are equipping more clients to integrate their existing operations with emerging digital strategies more seamlessly, efficiently and transparently across the full asset lifecycle.”
A foundation for digital asset innovation
Digital Asset Custody is the foundation of BNY’s digital asset capabilities, supporting use cases across digital cash, tokenized assets, payments, settlement, and collateral mobility across the financial ecosystem.
"With our central role and scale across capital markets, BNY is committed to building the financial infrastructure of the future in partnership with our clients," said Carolyn Weinberg, Chief Innovation and Market Transformation Officer at BNY. "This expansion reflects our continued investment in BNY’s capabilities to connect traditional and digital financial ecosystems and develop solutions that unlock new forms of financial activity for our clients globally.”

title: Mastercard and Tamatem Level Up Gaming Payments in the Middle East and Africa
summary:
Mastercard and Tamatem, one of MENA’s leading mobile games publishers backed by Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO) and supported by Abu Dhabi Gaming (ADG) have joined forces to enhance in-app gaming experiences across Middle East and Africa. Under the collaboration, Mastercard Gateway, available via Mastercard Merchant Cloud, will become the payment gateway behind Tamatem Plus, Tamatem’s white-label digital commerce platform and marketplace, in more than 13 markets across the Middle East and Africa, starting with Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
According to a recent report, the value of the MENA region’s gaming market reached around $7.1 billion in 2025, rising by 7.5% year on year. By combining expertise, the organizations are providing an enhanced checkout experience to players, while providing game publishers with a direct-to-consumer channel that enables them to  build stronger relationships with players, and gain greater control over brand and purchasing experiences.
The collaboration leverages Mastercard Gateway,  a global payment platform that enables secure transaction processing across multiple channels – from in-store to websites and mobile apps. Available through Mastercard Merchant Cloud, Mastercard’s unified, open acceptance framework, the platform provides a streamlined way for businesses to access modular payment solutions, such as agentic commerce, advanced fraud protection, authentication, tokenization, data and partner services – ultimately enabling merchants and businesses across MEA and beyond to scale faster, more securely and with less friction.  
“At Mastercard, we are committed to connecting people to their passions, and gaming is one of the fastest-growing passions in the region. Through meaningful partnerships, we are digitizing in-game payments to deliver unprecedented convenience to players and level up engagement. Tamatem is a remarkable local success story, and we are excited to combine our advanced technology and global network with their vision to unlock enhanced experiences for the gaming community ,” said Mete Güney, executive vice president, Market Development, EEMEA, Mastercard.
The collaboration will enable gamers to use Tamatem’s platform, Tamatem Plus where Players can check out through localized web stores and in-game checkout experiences using cards, local alternative payment methods and telco wallet balances, with authentication and fraud protection built in “When we started Tamatem in 2013, our belief was simple: MENA deserves world-class gaming built for our language and our culture. Together, we are making it simpler and more secure for every gamer in the region to play, pay and belong,” said Hussam Hammo, founder and CEO, Tamatem.

title: IMF warns tokenized markets could amplify financial risks
summary: The global financial institution found tokenized equity markets less liquid and more volatile than traditional markets, despite growing demand for 24/7 trading.
content: The International Monetary Fund has warned that tokenized markets could amplify financial risks globally. Despite the growing investor demand for round-the-clock trading, the global financial institution discovered that tokenized equity markets tend to be less liquid and significantly more volatile compared to traditional financial markets. Regulators are urged to monitor these emerging digital asset structures closely.

Bitcoin விலை $83,000-ஐ நோக்கி சரிந்து வருவதால், ஃபியூச்சர்ஸ் வர்த்தகர்கள் அதிகளவில் கரடி சந்தை (பேரிஷ்) நிலையை நோக்கிச் செல்கின்றனர். இந்த எதிர்மறை ஃபண்டிங் ரேட் என்பது ஷார்ட் பொசிஷன் வைத்துள்ளவர்கள் லாங் பொசிஷன் வைத்துள்ளவர்களுக்கு கட்டணம் செலுத்துவதைக் குறிக்கிறது, இது சந்தையில் ஷார்ட் எக்ஸ்போஷருக்கான தேவை அதிகரித்து வருவதைக் காட்டுகிறது.

content_ta: நிதி சேவைத் துறையில் பெரும்பகுதி AI பற்றிய உரையாடல் ஆட்டோமேஷன் மற்றும் செலவுக் குறைப்பு மீதே கவனம் செலுத்தியுள்ளது. இருப்பினும், Spade நிறுவனத்தைச் சேர்ந்த Oban MacTavish, வங்கிகள் மிகப்பெரிய வாய்ப்பை தவறவிடக்கூடும் என்று கூறுகின்றனர். நிதி நிறுவனங்கள் எளிய செலவுக் குறைப்புக்குப் பதிலாக வருவாயை அதிகரிக்க AI தொழில்நுட்பத்தைப் பயன்படுத்துவதன் மூலம் அதிக பலன்களைப் பெறலாம்.

title: Is XRP Decentralized? Cyber Capital Founder Says It's 'Straight-Up Fraud'
